text: Happy January Brothers! This is your friendly, and now current, ARO Nick Ness sending you the news and happenings of our beloved Beta Sigma Chapter! I would like to start off by saying I hope the New Year is treating all of you well! Before I update all of you on the chapter, I’d like to do a brief introduction. As you have seen now, this is Nick Ness. A change of office happened, and I was graciously nominated and voted into the ARO position by the chapter! For anyone who doesn’t know me very well, or at all, I was initiated in Fall of 2010. I spent 5 years at Idaho and in the chapter. In my time with the chapter I served as President from 2012-14, ACPR from 2013-15, and FEO 2014-15. I graduated in Fall of 2014 (kept collegiate status for Spring of ’15) with a B.S. in Geography and a minor in Climate Change. I moved back to Mukilteo, WA which is about 20 miles north of Seattle in June of ’15 and have been here since. I am now back in school earning a BAE in Special Education with an endorsement in Elementary Education with Western Washington University. I’ll graduate that program Winter Quarter of 2019. And now, here we are, your newly elected ARO for the rest of this academic year. For all of you, I want you to know that although I do not live in Moscow anymore, I have made arrangements with a couple collegiate brothers to get updates via phone and video chat. I am going to take this office seriously and do my best to keep our amazing alumni informed! Please feel free to reach out to me if you would like to know anything more than what is mentioned, request information to be added in the monthly newsletter, or if you have any other comments, questions, or concerns. I plan on sending out this monthly newsletter around the middle of each month for the rest of the year, so be on the look out! One goal that I would like to set for us alumni is to interact more (via Facebook, Calls, Video Chats, in person, or other means not mentioned) with the chapter. I know we all, as alumni, are busy doing so many amazing things, but even small hello’s can make a presence and a difference! I strongly feel that a general, yet strong alumni presence would be very beneficial to the chapter and open up possible resources that may have seemed closed up because current collegiate brothers may not know our band of alumni brothers. Our “Alumni” (really every chapter brother, alumni or not) Facebook page doesn’t seem to get much attention anymore, and that is a prime way to reach out for many if anything comes up! Again, feel free to reach out to me, too, if you don’t feel like posting on Facebook or have anything you’d like to see in the newsletters! Now, for the newsletter part! Each newsletter will have information on what the chapter is up to and what they have done, chapter birthdays (and hopefully alumni birthdays if I can get that organized enough!), future events for the chapter, and any other information that may come up. I would also like to feature one or two alumni and collegiate members in each newsletter, so be on the lookout for a message from me! As per usual, the first three day weekend in January is the observed Chapter Day and chapter lock-in, which was held on the 13th. I was lucky enough to Skype into the lock-in to meet everyone and chat for a bit! Prior to the actual lock-in, the chapter decided to hold the Chapter Day Ceremony and chapter meeting. Everyone had a great time, and maybe some alumni could go next year, too! IMEA All-State is coming up next week. The chapter will be volunteering for the event on Wednesday, January 31st from 3:00-6:00pm. If you are around, please come say hello to the brothers! There will be four different venues, 1 in Pullman and 3 in Moscow. The brothers will be in letters or may be wearing a Phi Mu Alpha name tag. Brothers will continue to volunteer as they are able through the rest of the event, February 1-3. If you happen to desire to volunteer also, you can reach out to me, and I will get you any information you will need for dates and times. Scrubfest and Audition Day is also coming up in the near future! The chapter will also be volunteering for this event. Volunteers are always needed, as I’m sure you all remember, so if you are interested in volunteering reach out to me again. Scrubfest is Friday night, February 9th. Please note that this is also a double header night for basketball. There is a game at 5:00pm and directly after at 7:30pm. So if you are in town and not going to the game, the chapter would greatly appreciate any support! Valentine’s Day is also just around the bend! Last year, the Washington Alpha Colony at WSU did a Valentine’s Choir for Hire fundraiser. Beta Sigma is planning to do the same or a similar set-up this year! Details are still to be determined, but what a great way to get the fraternity’s name out there and advertise the amazing things our chapter does on campus! Brother, Jason Svedberg is setting up a choir of brothers to sing the National Anthem at one or more of the upcoming basketball games. If you are interested in joining in, and you will be in the area for the games, contact him at: sved1555@vandals.uidaho.edu. The arrangement being worked on is the one directly out of our red song books. The chapter is also looking for more arrangements to sing! Many old arrangements have been lost through the years, and they need our help. If you still have an old arrangement of any pop tunes, or other music we performed, let’s send them they way of the chapter so they can be revived! That being said, if you would like to help the chapter by arranging any fun pop tunes and sending it their way, that would be just as great! Send arrangements to BetaSigmaBulls@gmail.com. One major piece of information is that Brother Jon Madrid, who currently holds the FEO position, has made the difficult choice to step down from the office. There are two nominees: Jason Svedberg and Max Justice. This new officer will be voted on in the next chapter meeting. 	Here is a current list of officers: 	President: Devin Funderburg 	VP: Max Justice 	Secretary: Tarrin Funderburg 	Treasurer: Logan Finney 	FEO: Jon Madrid (New officer TBD) 	Warden: Linn Bartel 	ARO: Nick Ness (Alumni status) One last piece of information I would like to have, I must ask from you. I would like to list birthdays in each newsletter for that month. For next month’s newsletter, I would like to have any alumni that has a birthday anywhere in the months of August through February (to catch up quickly), please respond to this newsletter with your birthday! Thanks for listening Brothers! Below, you will find my contact info if you need or want to reach out to me or the chapter. Nick Ness Fall ‘10 Phi Mu Alpha Sinfonia Alumni Relations Officer BetaSigmaAlumni@gmail.com BetaSigmaBulls@gmail.com
